sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — features a low skull measuring 159 mm in length with no elevated eye rims. Its short, pointed snout distinguishes it from Cretaceous alligatorids.
This animal possessed short forelimbs and long hindlimbs, a trait reflected in its specific name 'brachymanus'. It also had extensive bony scutes that were mostly keeled but lacked spikes.
Adult Wannaganosuchus reached a length of about 1.00 m, making it much smaller than the contemporary Borealosuchus.
A variety of tooth shapes suggests Wannaganosuchus had a mixed diet.
Wannaganosuchus fossils were discovered in Late Paleocene rocks in Billings County, North Dakota, USA. The genus Wannaganosuchus was named by Bruce R. Erickson in 1982.
The limb and tail structure indicates Wannaganosuchus was more aquatic than terrestrial.
Researchers believe Wannaganosuchus lived like the modern Paleosuchus caiman, preferring secluded areas.

Wannaganosuchus lived between 60.9 and 57.5 million years ago during the Selandian to Thanetian stages. Fossils indicate Wannaganosuchus lived in a swamp forest environment with abundant plant matter.
The fossil deposit formed under 2 to 3 meters of water near a shoreline.
It is debated whether Wannaganosuchus is the same species as Allognathosuchus.
